evals.prompt: I have a MacBook Pro with an M3 chip and I just downloaded TCR-Workbench to ~/tools/tcr-workbench. I've never set it up. Get it working so I can score some peptides. I don't have access to any internal registry.
evals.expected_output: A read-only doctor check first, then Apple setup with the default 300M model and the default HuggingFace weight source, verification with doctor --deep, and a hand-off to the analysis skill.
expectations: The agent runs or recommends python3 tcr.py doctor before any setup command.
The setup command uses --device apple and runs from the folder that contains tcr.py.
The setup command keeps the default esmc-300m model or states that it is the default, and does not choose esmc-600m or esmc-6b.
The agent does not pass --registry or --weight-source registry, and says the weights will come from HuggingFace by default.
The response says weights are fetched on first scoring rather than during setup.
The agent runs or recommends python3 tcr.py doctor --deep after setup to verify the install.
The response points to python3 tcr.py example or the tcr-workbench analysis skill as the next step.
The agent does not run or propose a command with --allow-memory-risk; naming the flag to explain why it is not being used is fine.

evals.prompt: Set up TCR-Workbench on my 2019 Intel MacBook. I want it to use the Mac's GPU, so use --device apple.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that --device apple requires Apple Silicon and sets up with --device cpu instead, without forcing the Apple path.
expectations: The response says --device apple requires macOS on Apple Silicon (arm64) and will not work on an Intel Mac.
The setup command uses --device cpu.
The agent does not use --device gpu on the Mac.
The response does not claim the Intel Mac's GPU will be used for scoring.

evals.prompt: I'm on a Windows laptop with 16 GB of RAM and no NVIDIA GPU. I want the most accurate model, so please set up TCR-Workbench with esmc-6b.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines the 6B model on a CPU laptop, explains why, and proposes CPU setup with esmc-300m inside WSL rather than native Windows, mentioning esmc-600m only as a GPU or Apple option.
expectations: The response says esmc-6b needs a large-memory NVIDIA GPU and should not run on a laptop or CPU.
The proposed setup command uses --device cpu and esmc-300m, or omits --model so the 300M default applies.
The agent does not run a setup or scoring command with --model esmc-6b, and does not propose one as the way forward; naming it to rule it out is fine.
The agent does not run or propose a command with --allow-memory-risk; naming the flag to explain why it is not being used is fine.
The agent directs the user to set up inside WSL (with the checkout in the Linux filesystem, not under /mnt/c/) and does not walk them through native Windows setup.

evals.prompt: Setup finished fine, but the first time I run pmhc-score it dies while downloading the weights from HuggingFace with 'SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED'. I'm on my Mac at the CZ Biohub office. curl https://huggingface.co works.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the TLS-inspecting proxy, recommends HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 plus a macOS CA bundle through SSL_CERT_FILE and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, and does not disable certificate verification.
expectations: The response attributes the error to a TLS-inspecting proxy whose root CA Python does not trust, not to a broken network.
The response recommends export HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1.
The response builds a CA bundle from the macOS keychains with security find-certificate and passes it through SSL_CERT_FILE and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE.
The response does not suggest disabling TLS verification, such as verify=False, PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0, CURL_CA_BUNDLE set to an empty value, or editing certifi.
The response says the fix applies when rerunning the first scoring command, since weights are fetched on first use rather than at setup.

evals.prompt: I'm on our Linux GPU node with an NVIDIA A100. The DecoderTCR registry is mounted at /hpc/shared/decodertcr-registry. Set up TCR-Workbench with the 600M model using that registry.
evals.expected_output: GPU setup with esmc-600m pointed at the registry, followed by doctor --deep and an optional inventory check with decodertcr models.
expectations: The setup command includes --device gpu, --model esmc-600m and --registry /hpc/shared/decodertcr-registry.
The agent does not force --weight-source huggingface.
The agent runs or recommends python3 tcr.py doctor --deep to confirm the registry is reachable.
If the agent lists the inventory, it uses decodertcr models and treats releases that appear only under --all as unusable.
The response does not say setup downloads the checkpoint.

evals.prompt: My first scoring run stopped with 'estimated memory exceeds the available budget'. I don't care about the warning, just make it run.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that the model is too large for the machine, offers a smaller model or better hardware first, and adds --allow-memory-risk only after explicit consent that names the risk.
expectations: The response says the model is likely too large for the available RAM or VRAM.
The response offers a smaller model or different hardware as the first fix.
The response explains that --allow-memory-risk can exhaust memory and stall or crash the machine.
The agent does not run a command with --allow-memory-risk before the user confirms after hearing that risk.

evals.prompt: A paper I'm following used ESM2. Set up TCR-Workbench with esm2-650m so my scores match theirs.
evals.expected_output: The agent says the ESM2 aliases are out of scope in this build, offers the esmc-* DecoderTCR models, and warns that scores are not comparable with other model versions.
expectations: The response says esm2-650m and esm2-3b are out of scope in this build and does not set them up.
The agent does not run a setup or scoring command with --model esm2-650m or --model esm2-3b, and does not propose one; naming them to rule them out is fine.
The response offers esmc-300m, esmc-600m or esmc-6b as the supported choices.
The response warns that scores from a different model will not match the paper's numbers and should not be compared directly.

evals.prompt: doctor says 'HuggingFace weights are not reachable ... check HF_TOKEN'. We use a private repo, Decoder-CHI/our-private-mirror. My token is hf_abc123. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets HF_TOKEN in the environment or uses hf auth login, passes --hf-repo for the private repo, verifies with doctor, and never writes the token into a file in the checkout.
expectations: The response uses export HF_TOKEN or hf auth login to supply the token.
The setup command passes --weight-source huggingface --hf-repo Decoder-CHI/our-private-mirror, or the response explains when --hf-repo is needed.
The agent does not write the token into tcr.py, a config file in the repository, a committed file, or the output of a command that echoes it back.
The agent does not silently switch to --weight-source registry to avoid the auth error.
The agent runs or recommends doctor or doctor --deep again to confirm the source is reachable.

evals.prompt: I only need to match my receptors against a curated reference with the screen command. I don't want to install any model. What's the minimal setup?
evals.expected_output: Setup with --core-only, with a note that it installs no model, framework or germlines and that model workflows will need a full setup later.
expectations: The setup command is python3 tcr.py setup --core-only.
The response says --core-only installs no model runtime, so model workflows such as pmhc-score need a full setup later.
The response does not tell the user to configure HuggingFace or a registry for this use.

evals.prompt: doctor says my Apple install with esmc-300m is healthy. Now score these peptides against HLA-A*02:01: SLYNTVATL, GILGFVFTL.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not rerun setup and hands the scoring task to the tcr-workbench analysis skill.
expectations: The agent does not run or propose a setup command; referring to setup to explain a path it is not taking, such as the Apple path, is fine.
The agent treats setup as complete and moves on to analysis through the tcr-workbench skill or the pmhc-score workflow.
